4 November 2026 · Structured-note optimization

Compact notes that track meeting changes

Main findings

  • Source notes cut earlier generated tokens by 59% and total generated tokens by 42% relative to old notes. Evidence
  • Thinking with source notes plus the focused prompt answers 11/12 and 9/12; reactive with that prompt answers 10/12 and 9/12. Evidence
  • Request-time thinking is essentially unchanged against focused reactive prompting, while total generation costs about 2.6 times as much. Evidence
  • Event fields propagate unsupported reasons and file-state claims; original-source notes preserve evidence more safely. Evidence

Project checklist · Daily log · Earlier S2 results

1. Source notes and event changes

The model selects useful transcript segments and links related statements. The program copies the selected words, speaker labels and source times into one bounded note state. The next update receives the new speech and the current state. At question time, the thinker receives the full available transcript and the latest notes.

Table 1. Inputs and outputs of the selected system.
ModuleInputOutput
Transcript boundaryExisting 25–40 s boundaries, within the requested 10–40 s range.Newly available transcript segments; the original schedule is shared across conditions.
Source selectorNew transcript, up to ten seconds of earlier reference speech and one note state.Source IDs, categories, priorities and links; no generated factual prose.
Context and revision checksSelected segments, nearby past speech and proposed revision links.Program-copied neighboring speech; the same model checks each proposed revision in a separate short call.
Note storeAccepted sources and relationships.At most 64 source segments, 20 visible links and 4,096 compact-JSON tokens; full source and link history remains on disk.
Question-time thinkerFull transcript, latest note state and the user question.Brief answer, source IDs and any missing information; Thinking exposes its native reasoning-token count.

A link can say revises, confirms, explains, qualifies or refers to. A revised deadline retains both the earlier and later statement. A different task keeps its own deadline. “I uploaded it” and “I cannot see it” remain separate claims until speech establishes what happened.

The selector skips greetings, routine acknowledgements and repeated facts without a change. Nearby source context helps preserve pronouns, unfinished clauses and qualifications. Exact source IDs are stored once per state; repeated speech in distinct source segments can still remain. The token limit removes lower-priority older sources first and favors recent revision endpoints.

Worked example: “Maya will prepare the sensor shipment. It should leave on Wednesday.” followed by “Change the sensor shipment to Thursday. Omar will handle it instead of Maya.” should retain the original assignment and its revision; an invoice due Monday remains a separate task. These names and values occur in a control test after the design was frozen.

2. Matched comparison

  • Use six development questions from five meetings, then freeze the policy before twelve additional questions from six other meetings.
  • Generate the additional-meeting notes with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and reuse identical notes for both Instruct and Thinking thinkers.
  • Keep the full transcript and the original answer prompt; test a focused thinker instruction both with and without notes.
  • Use greedy Instruct decoding and two Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 request seeds, 23 and 47.
  • Keep each note update question-blind and count all earlier writer and revision-check work.
Table 2. Five conditions on the twelve additional questions.
ConditionQuestion-time inputEarlier model work
ReactiveFull transcript + question.None.
Old notesFull transcript + question + all accumulated structured snapshots.Original full-prefix and earlier-snapshot prompting, rerun with the same Instruct writer.
Source notesFull transcript + question + one selected source-note state.Incremental source selection, context copying and revision checks.
Reactive + focused promptReactive input + the focused thinker instruction.None.
Source notes + focused promptSource-note input + the same focused thinker instruction.The same saved source-note run.

This study reviews 570 generated answers across 18 distinct questions and 11 meetings; repeated conditions and seeds account for the larger output count.

Scoring: Codex compares the final answer with previously reviewed required facts and source evidence. A complete answer contains the required facts and no material unsupported factual claim. Partial answers, incorrect answers and empty answers are retained. Citation format, source-ID validity and note-schema validity are audited separately. Additional-meeting answer packets hide the model and condition during review; this is not an independent human assessment.

The office-headcount reference was corrected from eighteen to fifteen after reviewing the later distinction between eighteen positions and fifteen people. The LCD-chip reference now includes an earlier statement that it is more expensive, while the amount remains unknown. The remote-control scope reference now retains the later TV-only backup and tentative reconsideration. Every condition uses the same corrected references; frozen model inputs and prompts are unchanged.

For the profit question, a bare 50% calculation is recorded as partially correct unless it retains the production-cost cap and before-other-costs qualification. The raw arithmetic and review reason remain visible.

Token accounting: request-time thinking tokens are native reasoning tokens generated after the question. Earlier reasoning and note output are amortized-thinking costs. Instruct has no exposed native thinking channel. Total generated tokens include all earlier output, request-time reasoning, answer JSON and delimiters. Input tokens count the logical prompt size, including cached tokens. CPU copying generates no model tokens; copied text counts whenever it enters a later prompt. Writer work is counted once per meeting through its latest tested request, and the two thinker seeds share the same saved notes.

Thinker output limits are 2,048 tokens for Instruct and 16,384 for Thinking. The Instruct writer has a 2,048-token cap; revision checks have a 64-token cap. The model context is 65,536 tokens and no input is silently trimmed. The additional questions were selected by meeting split and request timing; they cover EN2004a, EN2006b, ES2003c, ES2006a, ES2007a, IB4003.

With the original thinker prompt, Instruct gives 9/12 complete answers with source notes and old notes, versus 7/12 reactively. Adding the focused instruction gives 9/12 both with and without source notes.

Thinking gives 10/12 and 9/12 with source notes, compared with 9/12 in both reactive seeds and 8/12 in both old-note seeds. With the focused prompt, source notes give 11/12 and 9/12, versus 10/12 and 9/12 without notes. These are repeated runs of the same twelve questions.

The focused prompt has the clearest request-budget effect. Mean native thinking falls from 1,976 to 1,782 tokens reactively and from 2,048 to 1,783 with source notes, averaging the two seeds. Source notes therefore add no stable request-time saving over the matching focused reactive control.

Source-note construction uses 35,067 generated tokens versus 85,597 for the old writer. Including the Thinking thinker, mean total generation falls from 104.8k to 60.7k with the original prompt. Source notes with focus use 57.4k versus 22.3k for focused reactive prompting; logical input totals are 786.5k versus 85.8k tokens.

The office count illustrates a useful memory effect: plain source notes recover fifteen people in both Thinking seeds, while reactive and old-note thinkers repeat eighteen. Instruct still answers eighteen despite retaining the later clarification and revision link. The focused source thinker recovers fifteen in one seed and repeats eighteen in the other.

Across the twelve Instruct request inputs, old notes contain 2,114 exact repeated fact entries among 2,296 entries. Source notes contain two repeated text strings among 639 note entries, with unique source IDs in each state. This counts exact repetition after case/punctuation normalization; paraphrased repetition is not measured.

4. Existing automatic transcripts

The same frozen source-note policy is tested on the original six questions using the existing Parakeet and Whisper transcripts and anonymous speaker labels. The question is supplied as text. Reference identities are mapped only for scoring; the model receives automatic labels. Transcript boundaries and recognition outputs are unchanged.

Table 5. Six-question automatic-transcript comparison; Thinking values list seeds 23 and 47 in that order.
TranscriptThinkerPromptReactive completeSource notes completeMean request thinking: reactive → notes
ParakeetInstructOriginal4/64/6Unexposed → Unexposed
ParakeetInstructFocused4/64/6Unexposed → Unexposed
ParakeetThinkingOriginals23: 4/6; s47: 4/6s23: 4/6; s47: 5/61,712; 1,843 → 2,114; 1,770
ParakeetThinkingFocuseds23: 4/6; s47: 4/6s23: 5/6; s47: 4/61,892; 1,528 → 1,946; 2,040
WhisperInstructOriginal4/64/6Unexposed → Unexposed
WhisperInstructFocused4/64/6Unexposed → Unexposed
WhisperThinkingOriginals23: 4/6; s47: 5/6s23: 4/6; s47: 4/61,743; 1,754 → 1,584; 1,831
WhisperThinkingFocuseds23: 4/6; s47: 4/6s23: 4/6; s47: 6/61,866; 1,955 → 1,768; 1,722

Instruct remains at 4/6 with both transcripts and all four prompt/note conditions. Source notes do not resolve its stale outreach time or overstatement of file actions.

Thinking results vary by transcript and request seed. Parakeet source notes give 4–5/6 versus 4/6 reactively; Whisper source notes give 4/6 versus 4–5/6 reactively. Source notes with the focused prompt reach 6/6 in one Whisper seed and 4/6 in the other.

With the original thinker prompt, source notes increase mean request thinking by about 9% for Parakeet and reduce it by about 2% for Whisper. Including earlier writing, generated-token totals are about 2.2–2.4 times the corresponding reactive totals across these automatic-transcript conditions.

Recognition errors can change the event itself: the ground-truth failed-action phrase “I can’t cut and paste it into the other folder” becomes “I can kind of paste it into the other folder” in the Whisper input. Several thinkers then invent a completed move or a filename-based resolution.

Original transcript-quality analysis and WER · Speaker labels and reference identity matching

5. Retaining event changes and limiting repetition

All checked source-note words, speaker labels and times match available transcript segments, with unique IDs and bounded states. The three new-value controls retain the needed evidence; two have the expected direct revision links. The access test misses a direct visibility-to-access revision link.

6. Selecting evidence or interpreting the current state?

A follow-up returns to the six development questions. The same Thinking thinker receives either original-source notes or the already generated event fields, which contain short owner, deadline, status and access values with a change history. Both note sets were generated by Instruct before their questions were supplied. The full transcript and thinker settings remain the same. This exploratory check was added after freezing the main design.

Table 7. Matched six-question Thinking-thinker check; paired values list seeds 23 and 47. Earlier writing counts once for each condition.
Content and promptComplete / 6Mean request thinkingEarlier generatedTotal generated
Reactive4/6; 6/62,014; 1,672012,684; 10,710
Event fields5/6; 4/62,164; 2,76110,28123,938; 27,465
Source notes5/6; 5/61,927; 2,17811,18723,398; 24,821
Reactive + focused prompt5/6; 6/61,846; 2,198011,585; 13,828
Event fields + focused prompt5/6; 4/62,294; 3,02510,28124,697; 29,000
Source notes + focused prompt5/6; 4/62,552; 2,27311,18727,011; 25,355

With the original prompt, event fields give 5/6 and 4/6 complete answers with mean request thinking of 2,164 and 2,761 tokens. Source notes give 5/6 in both seeds with 1,927 and 2,178 tokens. Reactive gives 4/6 and 6/6 with 2,014 and 1,672 tokens. Neither memory format consistently improves accuracy and request thinking together.

The event fields contain an unsupported redundancy/no-benefit reason for dropping audio work. Three Thinking answers repeat this reason. Another answer turns “Move to meeting room” into a completed file relocation. These errors show why interpreting a current state needs checks on the field values, beyond valid source IDs.

The results favor one compact source-backed state over repeated generated snapshots as the next memory baseline. They do not yet establish that the saved notes perform enough useful reasoning to reduce the remaining request-time thinking. A useful next test is a small set of verified owner, time, quantity and status updates, with original evidence retained for uncertainty and revisions.

Input transcripts and requests · Selected complete model calls, including reasoning text · All answer and token records

Appendix A. Development and selection

Repeated snapshots enlarged the thinker input without consistently adding facts. Compact replacement and incremental edits reduced copying, but generated prose could merge tasks, invent a field value or retain an old deadline. Source-only storage was selected because it preserved critical evidence while reducing writer output.

On the six development questions, the selected source notes reduced earlier generated tokens from 29,735 to 11,187, including seven revision checks, and earlier input tokens from 271,613 to 165,279. Instruct improved from four to five complete answers. The latest outreach time was present in the notes, yet the thinker still answered with the older end-of-week time. Source retention and successful use are evaluated separately.

      "kind": "decision",

      "end": 137.85,

      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",

      "start": 162.69,
      "end": 169.04,

      "id": "ES2002b-U00013",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 50.55,
      "end": 62.94,
      "text": "Um kind of uh got to know each other a little bit and uh got familiar with all the equipment and started to discuss um a bit about the project, you know, cost-wise how much"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00014",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 62.94,
      "end": 64.14,
      "text": "how much money we had to s"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00015",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 100.92,
      "end": 113.0,
      "text": "Um just want to tell you that you have three new requirements, um which is the The first one is that um uh the company's decided that teletext is outdated uh"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00018",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 114.79,
      "end": 121.94,
      "text": "Nobody uses teletext very much anymore, so we don't really need to consider that in the functionality of the of the remote control."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00016",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 113.0,
      "end": 114.79,
      "text": "because of how popular the internet is."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00019",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 121.94,
      "end": 130.69,
      "text": "Um they've also suggested that we um we only use the remote control to control the television, not the V_C_R_, D_V_D_ or anything else."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00021",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 130.69,
      "end": 141.68,
      "text": "I think the worry is that if the project becomes too complex then it'll affect um how long it takes us to get it into into production, the time to market."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00022",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 141.68,
      "end": 145.41,
      "text": "So um, we're just gonna keep it simple and it'll just control the T_V_."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00023",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 145.41,
      "end": 150.49,
      "text": "And the other thing was that the company want the corporate colour and slogan to be implemented in the new design."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00024",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 151.21,
      "end": 154.97,
      "text": "Um I'm not entirely sure what the corporate colour is."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00025",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 154.97,
      "end": 158.12,
      "text": "It might be yellow, because there seems to be a lot of yellow everywhere."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00026",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 157.94,
      "end": 163.02,
      "text": "And the slogan, like the actual written slogan, or just to embody the idea of the slogan?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00030",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 167.0,
      "end": 179.3,
      "text": "uh th because on the the company website, uh what does it say Uh something Yeah, I mean do they Is that something they want actually written on it, 'cause it's quite long"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00032",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 180.07,
      "end": 182.3,
      "text": "Um or yeah, just the idea, but I'm not sure."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00028",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 172.4,
      "end": 174.07,
      "text": "'Bout putting the fashion in electronics."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00027",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 163.17,
      "end": 165.72,
      "text": "Well that's the thing, I'm I'm not sure um"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00034",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 183.96,
      "end": 196.19,
      "text": "So those are the three things, just not to worry about teletext, uh only control the T_V_, and um and uh incorporate the uh colour and slogan of the company"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00037",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 196.19,
      "end": 204.57,
      "text": "Um so is everybody okay with any of that, or do you want me to recap at all?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00036",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 202.95,
      "end": 203.98,
      "text": "Nope, we're all set."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00038",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 204.57,
      "end": 206.79,
      "text": "Right um, time for presentations then."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00040",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 210.36,
      "end": 210.79,
      "text": "I'll go first."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00043",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 217.21,
      "end": 219.91,
      "text": "Alright um, can I st steal this from the back of your laptop?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00045",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 219.83,
      "end": 221.38,
      "text": "Oh yeah, of course, yeah."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00046",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 221.38,
      "end": 222.11,
      "text": "G go on ahead."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00039",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 206.79,
      "end": 208.0,
      "text": "Who would like to go first?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00047",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 258.52,
      "end": 260.05,
      "text": "so this is the technical functions design."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00050",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 265.53,
      "end": 275.05,
      "text": "Right to do the um the design I have I've had a look online, I've had a look at the homepage, which has given us um some insp inspiration from previous products."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00051",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 275.05,
      "end": 284.6,
      "text": "Um I've had a look at the previous products to see what they offer and um I would like to ask you guys for um your ideas about the design at the end of the meeting."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00055",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 289.13,
      "end": 301.71,
      "text": "Um, having a look at the existing products, I found out that um it tends to come in sort of two extremes, there's either um a very complicated one that's got lots of buttons, lots of colours, very confusing, you don't know what you're doing"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00057",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 301.71,
      "end": 304.71,
      "text": "Um in that case the the labelling tends to be very bad."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2002b-U00052",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 284.6,
      "end": 287.7,
      "text": "Um unfortunately we're not allowed to talk outside the meeting room, so"
    }
  ],

TS3003b · 289.5 s
{
  "notes": [
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00009",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 77.26,
      "end": 89.53,
      "text": "Um important thing of this phase is that we're going to uh try to get an agreement about the user requirements, technical"
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00010",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 89.53,
      "end": 92.45,
      "text": "function design, and the working design."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00011",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 93.12,
      "end": 97.19,
      "text": "So that we can move onto the second uh phase."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00021",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 123.39,
      "end": 128.53,
      "text": "So it should be over in a in a while, couple of days."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00026",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 137.47,
      "end": 139.11,
      "text": "Uh this time I will take the minutes."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00029",
      "kind": "quantity",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 145.02,
      "end": 153.65,
      "text": "Um and we've got forty minutes for the whole uh prese for the whole uh presentations."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00020",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 121.57,
      "end": 123.39,
      "text": "It's in wing C_ and E_."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00023",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 128.53,
      "end": 134.39,
      "text": "But it's going to be cold anyway, so I don't think you're gonna need it."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00025",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 135.84,
      "end": 137.47,
      "text": "Now first the opening."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00027",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 140.36,
      "end": 143.75,
      "text": "Uh you're going to have a presentation."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00030",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 153.65,
      "end": 163.54,
      "text": "So uh I suggest we take about seven minutes per presentation, and then we can have a little discussion about the new project requirements uh which have been sent to me."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00031",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 164.39,
      "end": 172.91,
      "text": "And then the decision on the control functions uh which we wanna include and those which we don't wanna include."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00032",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 172.91,
      "end": 175.11,
      "text": "So we've got forty minutes for all of it."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00034",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 175.11,
      "end": 179.47,
      "text": "So I suggest um let's start with the first presentation."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00035",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 179.47,
      "end": 181.34,
      "text": "Um who wants to be first?"
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00036",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 182.76,
      "end": 183.55,
      "text": "Think I'll go first."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00039",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 187.94,
      "end": 193.37,
      "text": "Just maybe it's easier if you um Yeah I think you will tell your presentation as well."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00040",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 193.37,
      "end": 197.87,
      "text": "Just which function you have and what you're gonna talk about."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00042",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 206.85,
      "end": 208.13,
      "text": "My name is Freek Van Ponnen."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00043",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 208.13,
      "end": 209.65,
      "text": "I'm the Market Expert."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00045",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 212.1,
      "end": 214.26,
      "text": "Um I've done some research."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00046",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 214.26,
      "end": 223.02,
      "text": "We have we uh have been doing research in a usability lab where we observed um users operating remote controls."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00048",
      "kind": "quantity",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 225.56,
      "end": 228.22,
      "text": "We had one hundred of these uh test subjects."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00049",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 229.36,
      "end": 232.2,
      "text": "Uh in addition we did some market research."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00050",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 232.2,
      "end": 235.26,
      "text": "Uh see what the market consists of."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00047",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 223.02,
      "end": 225.56,
      "text": "Uh we let them fill out a questionnaire."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00044",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 209.65,
      "end": 210.91,
      "text": "But you already knew that."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00055",
      "kind": "quantity",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 250.97,
      "end": 256.33,
      "text": "people questioned uh indicated that they thought their remote were was ugly."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00056",
      "kind": "quantity",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 256.33,
      "end": 262.85,
      "text": "Um and an additional eighty percent indicated that they would spend more money on a fancy-looking remote control."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00054",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 247.53,
      "end": 249.63,
      "text": "F uh seventy five percent of the um"
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00059",
      "kind": "quantity",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 267.33,
      "end": 273.32,
      "text": "Fifty percent of the people indicated they only loo used about ten percent of the buttons on a remote control."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00060",
      "kind": "quantity",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 275.08,
      "end": 279.39,
      "text": "And fifty percent of the people indicated that their remote tended to get lost in their room."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00064",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 285.34,
      "end": 288.94,
      "text": "Then we did some research to the most relevant functions."
    },
    {
      "id": "TS3003b-U00058",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 264.67,
      "end": 267.33,
      "text": "Um in addition remotes were not very functional."
    }
  ],

    {

      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 162.52,
      "end": 173.82,
      "text": "Sometimes I have these pop-ups or these sounds and there's nothing there, and also with I don't know how to use PowerPoint, so it takes me forever to get something done with it."

      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 178.83,

      "text": "Here we go again."

      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 151.31,
      "end": 162.65,
      "text": "You can look at the final report, 'cause I have to record everything we are deciding and such, so I'm trying to write it down between everything else."

      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 182.84,
      "end": 193.83,
      "text": "Uh we have again three presentations and then we have to decide on what concepts the mobile phone has to uh f the remote control has to support."

      "text": "Me first again or yeah."

      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 223.43,

      "text": "So welcome to the marketing presentation once again."

      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 231.31,

      "text": "Uh well there has been inv investigation again, in the in the remote control market."
    },
    {

      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 236.5,

      "speaker": "D",

    {

      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 241.68,
      "end": 247.55,
      "text": "Um fashion watch watchers uh have detected the trends for young public, because that's our public."

    {

      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 247.92,
      "end": 255.09,
      "text": "Um well fruit and vegetables will be will be the most important theme for clothing, uh shoes and furniture."

      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 255.09,
      "end": 258.23,
      "text": "And the feel of the material is expected to be spongey."

      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 258.23,
      "end": 265.93,
      "text": "So um the developments I will address them oh yeah well this is the fruit and vegetables looks of fresh bright colours."

    {

      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 272.9,
      "end": 278.71,
      "text": "Uh well most important aspect for remote control happens to be a fancy look-and-feel."

      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 265.93,
      "end": 267.25,

      "end": 281.65,
      "text": "Instead of the current uh functional look-and-feel."

    {
      "id": "TS3006c-U00085",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 281.65,
      "end": 287.26,
      "text": "Um well fancy stands for an original look-and-feel of the case and the interface."

      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 287.74,
      "end": 295.76,
      "text": "And the second most important aspect is that a remote control should be technological uh innovative."

      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 295.76,

EN2004a · 615.5 s
{
  "notes": [
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00046",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 201.65,
      "end": 213.69,
      "text": "And so that um once you go through all the s um speech regions and all the um"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00048",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 213.69,
      "end": 225.93,
      "text": "non-speech regions, an o you could make another step of doing a search using um going under the edit menu you can do a search for, yeah, find"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00053",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 236.22,
      "end": 244.86,
      "text": "And then you can just resolve those all one by one as as a different set of um changes altogether."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00054",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 244.86,
      "end": 248.58,
      "text": "And and likewise for the double question marks."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00056",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 248.58,
      "end": 257.39,
      "text": "Just once you've gone through um and resolved all the open parentheses, you can do the same for op uh double question marks."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00057",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 257.39,
      "end": 264.1,
      "text": "And um and like I said, if you if you can't make any sense of it, then just use the at symbol."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00058",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 264.1,
      "end": 271.0,
      "text": "If you can um, just give it, you know, give it your best guess in these cases."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00061",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 270.83,
      "end": 282.95,
      "text": "How much should you want um I had a few times where I thought well, it could be this, but if you're not entirely sure that it could be, 'cause it c it could be a combination of something else, like put"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00065",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 286.41,
      "end": 296.63,
      "text": "Yeah, it's I would uh if you're v if you're quite certain, then I would go ahead and um type what you think it was said."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00067",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 296.63,
      "end": 305.11,
      "text": "If if you v think that n y there's maybe a th thirty percent chance you're wrong or or more"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00071",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 305.17,
      "end": 317.19,
      "text": "It's usually a context problem, because I think sometimes if it's not intelligible you either tend to because you really want it to fit the context, um you tend to take the closest actual word"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00072",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 317.19,
      "end": 327.95,
      "text": "that would fit the context, or if it sometimes it sounds very clear as a word itself, but then wouldn't make sense at all, and then you m question, you know, second-guess whether it's really what you heard."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00074",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 328.64,
      "end": 340.97,
      "text": "So maybe a good idea would be to listen to each channel one by one, do listen to the silent and non-silent regions and make all those corrections, leave the unknowns"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00075",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 340.97,
      "end": 346.05,
      "text": ", the um ambiguities, the uncertainties uncertainties until later."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00078",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 346.05,
      "end": 357.23,
      "text": "So go through all the channels and do that, and then um then you should have the context from all four speakers, and then go back and do those searches one by one for each channel."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00096",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 379.73,
      "end": 388.69,
      "text": "But if there's a chance that it's equally likely that they could have said something or they could have said something like ice cream and I scream, then just choose one and leave it, right."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00093",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 370.56,
      "end": 374.7,
      "text": "Yeah, I think that would be really helpful."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00097",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 387.59,
      "end": 392.26,
      "text": "Choose one, it c I mean y think of it from a speech recognition point of view again."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00103",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 395.62,
      "end": 407.76,
      "text": "What is most robust for a speech recognition and and leave out anything So you're well geared towards this task"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00112",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 416.91,
      "end": 422.45,
      "text": "Uh uh when I did my masters um I took uh S_P_ one and S_P_ two with Simon King."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00115",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 424.79,
      "end": 432.14,
      "text": "And actually I've done quite well in S_P_ one, I've done it a bit worse in S_P_ two because it was a l a lot more challenging."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00116",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 432.26,
      "end": 433.99,
      "text": "We have two new teachers for S_P_ two."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00121",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 437.01,
      "end": 444.45,
      "text": "And uh I'll ask you later on like if you still have your notes."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00126",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 449.87,
      "end": 452.4,
      "text": "I've just done one channel."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00129",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 456.12,
      "end": 460.76,
      "text": "'Cause I've got square brackets around all the things that need to be changed."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00130",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 460.76,
      "end": 467.25,
      "text": "Um so this person didn't ha um th obviously didn't know about capitalisation."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00131",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 467.25,
      "end": 472.05,
      "text": "So just about every utterance needs to be capitalised and and needs the end punctuation."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00133",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 472.16,
      "end": 484.53,
      "text": "You know, when you get like um someone's talking and there's they sort of pause in the middle of a sentence that's long enough for it to put a break in, but they're actually sort of carrying on the sentence, do you have to capitalise each time you transcribe"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00137",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 486.38,
      "end": 489.5,
      "text": "Whatever um makes sense to you."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00142",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 489.5,
      "end": 495.52,
      "text": "Um but no, it it can continue into the next segment and that's perfectly fine."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00146",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 495.05,
      "end": 500.95,
      "text": "I think that's actually the only case where you don't or where you're not supposed to capitalise, right?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00148",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 500.95,
      "end": 510.21,
      "text": "So if it's quite clear that the sentence is being carried on, the p you know, the sentence from the previous segment is being carried on, then that's when you don't capitalise."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00150",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 510.21,
      "end": 510.92,
      "text": "Otherwise you do."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00152",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 510.38,
      "end": 514.87,
      "text": "And you only use the hyphen I think when the sentence is definitely not continuing anywhere."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00159",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 516.11,
      "end": 521.77,
      "text": "I've done a few of those wrong then when someone comes to check it."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00160",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 519.92,
      "end": 526.19,
      "text": "I'll review some of these things um after I go through this a bit um just to re-cap."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00163",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 526.19,
      "end": 537.49,
      "text": "Th these are things that I've after checking um t everybody's work um, these are things that were commonly left out or, you know misc mis-transcribed, whatever."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00164",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 537.49,
      "end": 541.03,
      "text": "So I'll go over those t as an opportunity to use the white-board."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00166",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 544.08,
      "end": 556.28,
      "text": "So uh this person left out a lot of end punctuation and um here's a case where I think she was transcribing an out-breath um"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00167",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 556.28,
      "end": 560.61,
      "text": "or possibly an in-breath uh t uh in and used the hash mark."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00169",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 561.95,
      "end": 567.52,
      "text": "In any case, I didn't hear anything and and you shouldn't be transcribing in-breaths or out-breaths."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00172",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 578.55,
      "end": 579.76,
      "text": "It was the creaky voice."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00174",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 583.94,
      "end": 585.69,
      "text": "Creaky voice."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00176",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 585.69,
      "end": 587.23,
      "text": "But it is c really connected to the word."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00177",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 587.23,
      "end": 587.97,
      "text": "Can we hear it again?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00179",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 582.47,
      "end": 589.17,
      "text": "It was but it wa yeah, it was a bit of a yeah, it was creaky, so yeah f uh"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00180",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 588.56,
      "end": 593.29,
      "text": "And you sometimes you don't know really whether it's a mic noise or that person is making that noise."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00182",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 593.04,
      "end": 595.94,
      "text": "Yeah, well I didn't think it was im let's see, wait."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2004a-U00185",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 610.52,
      "end": 614.77,
      "text": "S there's there's actually quite a bit more in there than than I heard before."
    }
  ],

EN2006b · 420.5 s
{
  "notes": [
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00011",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 15.92,
      "end": 19.62,
      "text": "But I think maybe that one should be underlined."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00017",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 30.37,
      "end": 32.38,
      "text": "And they don't know what to do with the H_T_M_L_ goo."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00022",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 37.28,
      "end": 45.9,
      "text": "And this isn't a separate thing, so I w I would agree that you underline the you underline the goo in each case but not the and."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00027",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 46.23,
      "end": 48.71,
      "text": "Do you reckon this stands for lambda or yeah, okay."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00035",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 67.81,
      "end": 71.08,
      "text": "I think high excitation should be in because it's just saying"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00036",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 73.0,
      "end": 76.8,
      "text": "It's talking about the species that the emission lines are coming from."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00042",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 93.75,
      "end": 96.48,
      "text": "ESO, I don't think is an instrument."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00044",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 97.32,
      "end": 100.4,
      "text": "ESO isn't an instrument."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00046",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 108.52,
      "end": 111.56,
      "text": "We agreed for to keep hubble."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00048",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 111.49,
      "end": 113.59,
      "text": "To not yes, to keep hubble."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00049",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 113.59,
      "end": 116.62,
      "text": "Um for this that should be green as well."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00055",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 125.53,
      "end": 130.9,
      "text": "Yeah, I think it all is yeah, I think it is all m one name."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00058",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 128.43,
      "end": 131.97,
      "text": "Absorption line systems shouldn't be there."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00063",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 147.76,
      "end": 153.85,
      "text": "Needs column densities, which is a derived property."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00069",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 164.8,
      "end": 166.7,
      "text": "And Lyman alpha cloud shouldn't be in there either."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00070",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 166.99,
      "end": 167.17,
      "text": "Nope."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00084",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 188.68,
      "end": 195.97,
      "text": "I forgot to keep track of the overall score, like who wins and who lose."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00085",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 194.15,
      "end": 196.25,
      "text": "Bottle of champagne."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00086",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 197.41,
      "end": 198.57,
      "text": "I've labelled that wrong."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00092",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 211.49,
      "end": 215.26,
      "text": "But is emission line A_G_N_ a separate class from A_G_N_?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00095",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 218.27,
      "end": 219.02,
      "text": "I don't think it is."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00099",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 224.24,
      "end": 226.24,
      "text": "You can get A_G_N_ without emission lines."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00100",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 226.36,
      "end": 228.89,
      "text": "But I don't think you'd particularly class them as a separate source."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00102",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 233.97,
      "end": 234.68,
      "text": "Maybe you would."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00103",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 232.8,
      "end": 237.43,
      "text": "I think in Phil's paper he does, doesn't he?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00107",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 244.01,
      "end": 248.91,
      "text": "I've seen people talk about them as separate classes, but I don't really know what that means."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00109",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 248.87,
      "end": 254.95,
      "text": "And I guess there is a difference between uh an A_G_N_ with emission lines and one without, esp especially if it's X_ ray detected."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00112",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 254.95,
      "end": 261.43,
      "text": "So yeah, I'm happy with that as long as that's red as well, which it is."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00116",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 266.91,
      "end": 268.09,
      "text": "Oh, galactic stars."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00119",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 277.79,
      "end": 280.5,
      "text": "G_ dwarf."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00127",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 287.26,
      "end": 290.5,
      "text": "So 'cause our sun is a is a T_ dwarf."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00135",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 299.27,
      "end": 300.42,
      "text": "Absorption"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00136",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 301.75,
      "end": 304.95,
      "text": "By Lyman alpha forest and Lyman limit systems."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00137",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 303.46,
      "end": 305.51,
      "text": "But it's the same Lyman alpha forest systems again."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00140",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 310.51,
      "end": 312.78,
      "text": "Or there maybe there shouldn't be any yeah, I think should still be absorption."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00142",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 317.2,
      "end": 319.03,
      "text": "Radio loud quasar again."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00145",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 321.97,
      "end": 324.99,
      "text": "Emission models, definitely not."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00148",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 326.25,
      "end": 335.51,
      "text": "I should definitely now we had a debate about this before, and I can't remember why I decided to mark associated."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00150",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 335.51,
      "end": 337.5,
      "text": "Um what does it mean?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00151",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 338.66,
      "end": 345.62,
      "text": "It means it's associated with some physical thing, but it doesn't have anything to do with the spectral features, I don't think."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00154",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 347.38,
      "end": 349.43,
      "text": "What is as associated absorption?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00159",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 357.92,
      "end": 359.09,
      "text": "I don't know."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00161",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 360.95,
      "end": 364.86,
      "text": "I'm happy to say M_ two what-not absorption is a spectral feature."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00165",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 364.86,
      "end": 370.11,
      "text": "But associated means it's associated to some physical thing."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00169",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 370.15,
      "end": 371.0,
      "text": "I wouldn't have that."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00170",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 370.97,
      "end": 371.7,
      "text": "So that shouldn't be in."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00174",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 373.83,
      "end": 375.89,
      "text": "Um and associated again."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00176",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 382.82,
      "end": 384.44,
      "text": "Those are mechanisms."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00178",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 384.44,
      "end": 385.37,
      "text": "So they don't count."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00181",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 393.92,
      "end": 394.42,
      "text": "Quasar."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00182",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 393.89,
      "end": 394.97,
      "text": "Yep, I just missed it."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00184",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 397.3,
      "end": 401.0,
      "text": "And we should've s put emission line features, shouldn't we?"
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00186",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 401.47,
      "end": 402.05,
      "text": "Yeah, we should do."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00187",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 403.77,
      "end": 405.77,
      "text": "But we're not supposed to mark things we've done differently."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00189",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 406.72,
      "end": 409.02,
      "text": "Yeah, we did that the same."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00190",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 409.02,
      "end": 410.88,
      "text": "But it's different from what we've been doing."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00191",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 410.86,
      "end": 413.44,
      "text": "We've just talked about n und underlining features."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00192",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 411.97,
      "end": 417.24,
      "text": "Well I think y bu y y you can actually mark it if it isn't altering what's in the manual."
    },
    {
      "id": "EN2006b-U00194",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 417.24,
      "end": 419.7,
      "text": "Uh um it's only altering earlier rules."
    }
  ],

    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00005",

      "start": 36.79,
      "end": 48.01,
      "text": "L_C_D_ and a couple of other buttons for navigation um with power being I suppose one of the main single purpose buttons."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00006",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 48.01,
      "end": 60.87,
      "text": "Um we were also going to use novelty of being able to locate the remote control again via a small transmitter with any luck, the idea to try and separate us and also because of the minimal design um"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00007",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 60.87,
      "end": 68.33,
      "text": "looks like we'll be able to be fairly adventurous in the actual physical shape of our remote control with any luck."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00009",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 72.06,
      "end": 79.76,
      "text": "So we'll just crack on, um like to maybe start with the Industrial Designer if it's possible."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00012",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 79.76,
      "end": 84.2,
      "text": "Um uh the con today is the concep today."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00033",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 146.31,
      "end": 151.66,
      "text": "The case uh le that's what I wrote first of all, could be plastic our plastic."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00035",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 159.26,
      "end": 161.78,
      "text": "So uh we decide what it's gonna be."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00036",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 161.78,
      "end": 163.17,
      "text": "Probably plastic."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00038",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 165.16,
      "end": 167.63,
      "text": "we need the infra-red transmitter."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00039",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 167.63,
      "end": 168.75,
      "text": "Get that off the shelf."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00048",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 194.82,
      "end": 197.08,
      "text": "three different types of batteries."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00051",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 199.52,
      "end": 211.01,
      "text": "can either use a hand dynamo, or the kinetic type ones, you know that they use in watches, or else uh a solar powered one."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00057",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 219.48,
      "end": 227.36,
      "text": "Um the bat uh the battery for a a watch wouldn't require a lot of power, would be my one query."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00059",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 227.36,
      "end": 231.53,
      "text": "Is a kinetic one going to be able to supply enough power?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00065",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 236.02,
      "end": 238.74,
      "text": "Yeah, I don't think it would."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00070",
      "kind": "decision",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 247.99,
      "end": 251.15,
      "text": "We should probably just use conventional batteries."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00078",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 275.1,
      "end": 283.34,
      "text": "Um the materials are tha there as you can see, but uh you can't have a titanium one for a double curved, uh which would be"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00081",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 286.24,
      "end": 287.76,
      "text": "Is it not also it's expensive?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00082",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 288.37,
      "end": 290.83,
      "text": "Uh, i think so as well, yeah."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00089",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 295.22,
      "end": 302.95,
      "text": "Um, I don't know if you'd be able to off the top of your head or not, the single curved and double curved, would you be able to give an example?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00092",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 305.46,
      "end": 310.97,
      "text": "I you don't doesn't have to be perfect, it's just 'cause I'm not quite sure if I understand the difference between the two."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00100",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 333.28,
      "end": 337.88,
      "text": "an okay button around here, so that the thumb can uh use it quite easily."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00115",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 370.24,
      "end": 376.55,
      "text": "Um which obviously it looks better than the single curve, but uh you can't have it in titanium, which is"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00121",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 396.24,
      "end": 404.53,
      "text": "um it requires a more expensive chip to use, and if you wanna use L_C_D_ it's even more expensive."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00122",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 404.53,
      "end": 407.81,
      "text": "So you have to decide, there's trade-offs there."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00125",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 417.88,
      "end": 426.92,
      "text": "But you're gonna ha I reckon you're gonna have to have uh key a number keypad anyway for the amount of channels these days."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00128",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 432.49,
      "end": 438.16,
      "text": "So um I reckon we're gonna have to have a number keypad anyway."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00129",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 439.84,
      "end": 440.48,
      "text": "Do you think?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00130",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 441.2,
      "end": 447.45,
      "text": "Okay, that was definitely something we can talk about."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00131",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 447.45,
      "end": 452.98,
      "text": "Um so you've got a little bit about the the chip that we might require as well?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00134",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 457.53,
      "end": 458.27,
      "text": "depends where"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00137",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 468.42,
      "end": 478.46,
      "text": "Um, do you have any idea so far, like when we're saying that we'd need an advanced chip for an L_C_D_, does that in shoot the cost up by a drastic amount?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00135",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 460.66,
      "end": 461.63,
      "text": "gonna spend the money"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00139",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 478.79,
      "end": 481.18,
      "text": "Need an advanced chip for the L_C_D_."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00144",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 487.25,
      "end": 497.65,
      "text": "if you press a button that sends a certain transmission through the infra-red, whereas I think if we're controlling the L_C_D_ we definitely require a much more powerful chip."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00148",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 497.65,
      "end": 502.83,
      "text": "Just compared to the chip you would use for pushing buttons I think is the the point being made."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00140",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 481.18,
      "end": 481.74,
      "text": "Is that did I"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00149",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 502.83,
      "end": 504.52,
      "text": "If I've not over-stepped."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00143",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 486.27,
      "end": 488.78,
      "text": "Advanced, like three eight six advance."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00154",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 512.8,
      "end": 514.92,
      "text": "Mm, if we only have twelve Pounds fifty,"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00157",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 522.3,
      "end": 528.34,
      "text": "Well we'd also be relying on the um the bulk buying in producement and such."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00160",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 529.27,
      "end": 531.48,
      "text": "We have to look into the costs of those."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00153",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 506.3,
      "end": 510.21,
      "text": "Okay, um should I go on, or go back?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00155",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 516.16,
      "end": 518.45,
      "text": "twelve Euros, not even twelve Pounds."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00158",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 527.8,
      "end": 528.73,
      "text": "Okay, that's good point."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00156",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 518.45,
      "end": 521.42,
      "text": "Twelve Euros, what's that, like eight pounds or something like that, nine Pounds?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00163",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 539.64,
      "end": 548.6,
      "text": "If you go to the one before that uh so it just says what it does, translate the key press into an infra-red signal and this is received by the T_V_."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00164",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 548.6,
      "end": 556.33,
      "text": "Uh the chip just needs to detect the signal or detect the key press and then uh it'll send it to the tr the amplifier."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00162",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 532.47,
      "end": 539.64,
      "text": "Uh the previous slides just explain what's in the internal components of the uh remote control."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00167",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 564.85,
      "end": 568.73,
      "text": "uh interact with the buttons, the rubber buttons, uh"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00168",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 570.48,
      "end": 572.98,
      "text": "to uh get sent to the chip."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00170",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 580.49,
      "end": 584.23,
      "text": "Um we have to decide on what buttons we're gonna use."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00169",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 575.5,
      "end": 578.16,
      "text": "So that's just how the control works inside."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2003c-U00166",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 558.87,
      "end": 563.51,
      "text": "And uh then the next slide just shows how the uh copper wires"
    }

{
  "notes": [
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00105",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 469.23,
      "end": 473.41,
      "text": "And yeah um and I like cocktails, especially pink ones."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00108",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 473.99,
      "end": 476.24,
      "text": "Excellent, to match the rabbit."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00111",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 485.87,
      "end": 488.72,
      "text": "Um so my name is Maarika."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00116",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 502.48,
      "end": 514.66,
      "text": "Uh so um um I'm the Interface Designer in this project and my favourite animal, I m I mean I'm not so sure because I'm not so so very um familiar with all kinds of animals"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00117",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 514.66,
      "end": 516.14,
      "text": ", but I do like dogs."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00120",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 524.91,
      "end": 529.51,
      "text": "Um well, there are different kinds of dogs, but okay um."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00119",
      "kind": "context",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 516.14,
      "end": 521.74,
      "text": "Oh, sorry, maybe I should have shouldn't have said it beforehand but mm hmm."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00126",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 543.64,
      "end": 545.64,
      "text": "I think it needs four legs if it's gonna walk though."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00129",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 549.41,
      "end": 558.14,
      "text": "Um yeah and I do like dogs because they are good friends to people and they are loyal."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00122",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 538.74,
      "end": 541.39,
      "text": "That's not bad at all."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00135",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 577.98,
      "end": 581.84,
      "text": "Um what it has to do with with my role in the project is hard to say."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00137",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 581.84,
      "end": 595.21,
      "text": "Uh I hope to be loyal to the project and not to n not to um let people doing similar projects know the details of our project or something, yeah"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00143",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 602.41,
      "end": 615.18,
      "text": "Oh, right, my roles, um so um in the different um stages of the design, so at first I will be responsible for um for"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00144",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 615.18,
      "end": 628.01,
      "text": "yeah, designing the technical functions of the um um of the remote control uh then in the in the conceptual design stage I need to"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00145",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "D",
      "start": 628.01,
      "end": 638.45,
      "text": "um come up with uh interface concept and then in the last um stage I will be responsible for the int infa for the user interface design."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00150",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 653.53,
      "end": 659.57,
      "text": "I'll rub the features and let the drawing stay."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00151",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 660.86,
      "end": 662.63,
      "text": "'Kay um my name is Gaurav."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00152",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 668.95,
      "end": 675.2,
      "text": "Um my favourite animal one of my favourite animals is a cow."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00153",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 675.2,
      "end": 677.2,
      "text": "I've got no idea how to draw a cow."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00156",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 684.08,
      "end": 688.48,
      "text": "They're not just like a big round body and then some really skinny legs and then just some horns."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00157",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 687.43,
      "end": 688.55,
      "text": "Yeah, that'll do."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00158",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 688.55,
      "end": 690.41,
      "text": "Okay, so let let me draw the body first."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00160",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 692.04,
      "end": 701.69,
      "text": "Big, round body, really skinny legs and they've got a long tail and a long face."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00164",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 704.9,
      "end": 708.34,
      "text": "And there is some grass there."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00165",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 712.87,
      "end": 715.38,
      "text": "Horns, draw some horns."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00166",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 708.34,
      "end": 721.68,
      "text": "So this is what I like about cows that they just keeps sitting there eating grass, they do not disturb anybody um they're kind of Buddhist in a way"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00169",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 724.95,
      "end": 737.87,
      "text": "Um my my role in the project is um uh the industrial designer, so I'm supposed to design all the details of of the product um"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00170",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 737.87,
      "end": 750.18,
      "text": "ho how it works and whatever it'll mm take during the functional role, what are the various functions that have to be performed by it uh during the um conceptual design, what are the various components of it"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00171",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 750.18,
      "end": 755.26,
      "text": "and um finally, I'm not too sure what was the last part."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00172",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 755.26,
      "end": 762.78,
      "text": "Um the detailed design, I I guess it will again be the identification of the components and how they integrate with each other."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00174",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 766.93,
      "end": 773.3,
      "text": "Uh I'm doing my P_H_D_ in Psycholinguistics, I sit at the Department of Psychology."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00181",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "A",
      "start": 791.39,
      "end": 794.05,
      "text": "That doesn't look like a cow, does it?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00185",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 797.28,
      "end": 798.34,
      "text": "I'm Jen."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00187",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 799.64,
      "end": 805.98,
      "text": "Um I like dogs too, but I can't do that already because I can't draw a dog as well as you can."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00189",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "B",
      "start": 825.48,
      "end": 826.24,
      "text": "Is that a lizard?"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00193",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 837.53,
      "end": 838.29,
      "text": "It's a gecko."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00199",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 844.56,
      "end": 846.91,
      "text": "Yeah, they're l it's a kind of lizard."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00203",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 846.91,
      "end": 858.92,
      "text": "And I I like geckos because they remind me of warm places and, and where I was living in Cambodia they used to live in my house and they"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00205",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 858.92,
      "end": 863.41,
      "text": "were on the ceiling and they would make little gecko noises in the evening."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00207",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 865.0,
      "end": 865.94,
      "text": "I don't like snakes."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00209",
      "kind": "reason",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 865.94,
      "end": 868.71,
      "text": "I come from Australia and we have nasty snakes."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00213",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 871.71,
      "end": 884.07,
      "text": "I'm from Melbourne and I'm your Project Manager for today and my role is basically to keep things going"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00214",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 884.07,
      "end": 887.44,
      "text": "and make sure that you all work together"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00215",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 888.66,
      "end": 892.95,
      "text": "in a productive way, so that by the end of the day we come up with a great product."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00219",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 905.52,
      "end": 909.4,
      "text": "So, let's see what's next in the PowerPoint presentation."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00222",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 911.94,
      "end": 921.81,
      "text": "So, I've just thought yeah I've just thought about this that we could even put it much more professionally as there we go."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00226",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 938.27,
      "end": 943.34,
      "text": "Um we're planning to sell the remote controls for twenty five Euros each."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00227",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 944.61,
      "end": 949.95,
      "text": "Um and with that we're aiming for a profit of fifty million Euros."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00225",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 930.48,
      "end": 938.27,
      "text": "We've got um we're planning to sell these remote controls for let's make that go away, that means we've got five minutes."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00228",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 952.07,
      "end": 955.89,
      "text": "And that's selling them on the international market, not just in the U_K_."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00229",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 957.83,
      "end": 971.3,
      "text": "Um so to do that our finance people estimate that we need production costs of maximum twelve and a half Euro so that we can reach that profit"
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00230",
      "kind": "commitment",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 971.3,
      "end": 972.63,
      "text": "target."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00235",
      "kind": "constraint",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 1010.68,
      "end": 1012.84,
      "text": "We've only got a couple of minutes."
    },
    {
      "id": "ES2006a-U00236",
      "kind": "unresolved",
      "speaker": "C",
      "start": 1012.84,
      "end": 1021.29,
      "text": "Does anyone have any first ideas to bounce around about um what we're thinking of this remote control?"
    }
  ],
